---
title: "How do I predict an outcome using a fitted regression equation?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I predict an outcome using a fitted regression equation?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Fit the model with the original paired observations.

2. Provide a new data frame whose predictor name matches the model.

3. Request interval='prediction' and explain uncertainty.

## Runnable example

```{r}
distance_km <- c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8)
time_min <- c(4,6,9,11,14,16,18,21)
fit <- lm(time_min ~ distance_km)
new_case <- data.frame(distance_km=5.5)
print(predict(fit,newdata=new_case,interval="prediction"))
```

## Interpret the result

The fitted model predicts travel time at 5.5 km and reports a prediction interval for a new observation under its assumptions.

## Check before using real data

A prediction interval for a future observation is wider than a confidence interval for the mean response. Avoid unsupported extrapolation.
